walkthroughs.body_html:
Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Dialogue Between Religious & Non-Religious Beliefs — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Dialogue Between Religious & Non-Religious Beliefs brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: What is the focus of virtue ethics?
options: Hinduism worships no gods, only ancestors.
On character and habits — becoming the kind of person who acts well, aiming at eudaimonia (flourishing) through practising virtues that lie between extremes.
Virtue ethics tells you which specific actions are right and wrong.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.

Five distinct arguments for God's existence: from motion, causation, contingency, gradation of being, and final causes/teleology — collectively forming Aquinas's natural theology, not a single argument.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five steps of one cosmological argument.
Hinduism worships no gods, only ancestors.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
Hinduism worships no gods, only ancestors.
It is more accurately described as henotheistic or monistic — many gods (devas) are considered aspects or manifestations of one ultimate reality (Brahman).
Hinduism is straightforwardly polytheistic with millions of separate gods.
